 Entering an emotional weekend that saw the return of outside hitter Harper Murray to her home state, the Cornhuskers were pushed in their back-to-back matches against Michigan and Michigan State. Both the Wolverines and Spartans took the opening set, but NU responded in each circumstance with three-straight set victories to stay unbeaten and hold firm at the top of the Big Ten standings. 
--> Entering an emotional weekend that saw the return of outside hitter Harper Murray to her home state, the Cornhuskers were pushed in their back-to-back matches against Michigan and Michigan State. Both the Wolverines and Spartans took the opening set, but NU responded in each circumstance with three-straight set victories to stay unbeaten and hold firm at the top of the Big Ten standings. 
 Setter Bergen Reilly earned her 16th career Big Ten weekly honor after setting the Husker offense to a .380 hitting percentage. The South Dakota native averaged 12.88 assists per set in the two victories while thumping five service aces. She recorded a season-high 58 assists with nine digs and two aces against Michigan. She followed up with 45 assists, five digs, two kills and a career-best six blocks versus Michigan State to cap off the weekend.

 Caught by surprise with the departure of former head coach Matt Ulmer to Kansas, the Ducks pivoted to a standout from the West Coast Conference (WCC) in Loyola Marymount head coach Trent Kersten. Coming off a WCC title and coach of the year honors in 2024, Kersten timed his breakout season perfectly to align with the Oregon administration. The Ducks were lackluster in 2025 with a 17-13 record and in a tie for 10th in the Big Ten, but expectations were cooled knowing that Kersten built his first roster in short order.
